from.place: proof, induction step: the description of K_X and K_X(F) at the generic points (Stacks Tag 0EMH), using the weakly-associated-point and finite-component hypotheses of Tag 0EMF

title: Generic-point product description of the meromorphic sheaf
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let X^0 be the set of generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of X. Assume (a) every weakly associated point of X is the generic point of an irreducible component, where a point is weakly associated when the maximal ideal of its local ring is weakly associated to that local ring, meaning it is minimal among the prime ideals containing the annihilator of some element, and (b) every quasi-compact open of X has finitely many irreducible components. Let K_X be the sheaf obtained by localizing O_X at its non-zero-divisors, and let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For each generic point eta write j_eta: Spec(O_{X,eta}) \to X for the canonical morphism. Then K_X = product_{eta in X^0} j_{eta,*} O_{X,eta} and K_X(F) = K_X tensor_{O_X} F = product_{eta in X^0} j_{eta,*} F_eta.
